title: SIFMA-recommended US fixed-income early close, 2:00 p.m. ET — the last session of 2026, with equities open all day
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule', SIFMA's own US Holiday Recommendations panel), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,926 bytes) and parsed out of the page's embedded payload by this session. The US entry renders as three fields — heading 'New Year's Day 2026/2027', date 'Friday, January 1, 2027', note 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Thursday, December 31, 2026'. The same field shape reproduces across the panel (e.g. 'Christmas Day' / 'Friday, December 25, 2026' / 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Thursday, December 24, 2026'), so the note attaches to the holiday it precedes. Cross-checked against NYSE nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, re-fetched the same day (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes): its holiday grid carries exactly three early-close footnotes across 2026-2028 — the day after Thanksgiving in all three years, Monday 2028-07-03, and Thursday 2026-12-24 — and NO equity early close for 2026-12-31, so equities trade a full session to 16:00 ET that day. Filed estimate on three counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an industry trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and SIFMA's own press release states verbatim that its closes are 'recommendations only; each member firm should decide for itself whether its fixed income departments remain open for trading' and that 'all SIFMA recommendations are subject to change due to market conditions'
notes: DISCOVERED during the christmas-eve-half-day-2026-12-24 initial research (2026-09-05), while pairing NYSE's full early-close footnote set against SIFMA's US 2026 and 2027 panels rather than reading only the Christmas rows. Why it earns a row: it is the SECOND dated cross-asset schedule split in the same six-session corridor, and it runs the OPPOSITE WAY from the first. On 2026-12-24 equities stop at 13:00 ET while the recommended bond tape runs to 14:00 — the bond tape outlives the equity tape, which happens on only three dated sessions in the whole forward window (2026-11-27, 2026-12-24, 2027-11-26). Six sessions later, on this date, the asymmetry inverts to the ordinary shape: bonds shut at 14:00 ET while equities trade a full session to 16:00, so a cross-asset construction loses its bond-side reference two hours before the equity close. Reading the corridor as one configuration is therefore wrong in one direction or the other on one of the two days. It is also the LAST session of 2026 and the fifth and final session of the Santa Claus Rally window that the sibling ledger measures and refuses (SPY 1993-2025: 23 of 33 positive, 69.7%, against a 58.7% unconditional rolling-7-session control, one-sided binomial p = 0.134), so the window's closing print is taken on a session with an atypical cross-asset liquidity profile. IMPACT LOW AND STRUCTURAL ONLY: a recommended early close is not a market-wide halt, it moves nothing by itself, and no house playbook is calendar- or holiday-keyed (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md grepped for 'holiday|christmas|half-day|early close|closure|santa' this session: zero hits in both). It widens caution about the 12-31 afternoon and licenses nothing. HONEST LIMIT ON THE KIND FIELD: EventKind (src/domain/market-events-types.ts) has no market-structure member, so this is filed 'rates' — the closest fit, and the same choice sifma-bond-early-close-2027-03-25 already made for the identical shape; whether the union needs a 'market-structure' member is not this lane's call. SECOND HONEST LIMIT: whether CME's rate futures keep their own separate hours that afternoon is NOT asserted — cmegroup.com has returned HTTP 403 to this runner across every prior attempt in sibling lanes, and this session did not re-attempt it, so the futures leg is unresearched rather than assumed.
